tasks.short: Process supplier, agency, fee and tax invoices and release the payment batch.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice, a staffing-agency invoice, a fee, or a tax assessment arrives and is due for payment.
steps: Open the PDF from Outlook or the export from one of the three agency portals.
Check amount, VAT, IBAN and site against the purchase order, the goods receipt or the approved flex hours in AFAS.
Code the cost and the VAT treatment, including reverse charge on foreign transport, and code any Belastingdienst assessment against the return.
Clear mismatches with the bookkeeper or the site lead.
Put the item on the Rabobank payment batch and release it under the four-eye rule.
drudgery: Re-typing lines from PDFs and portal files.
Looking up the same agency surcharge and VAT codes every week.
Chasing missing site approvals by mail.
today.time_sinks: Disputed flex hours, invoices with no purchase order, and batches that have to be rebuilt after a wrong IBAN or VAT line.

lenses.faster: Keying, code lookup and the first match leave the accountant's day. Disputed hours, odd VAT lines, tax assessments and the Rabobank release remain, together about two fifths of the time this task takes today.
lenses.autonomous: An invoice in the AFAS inbox, the Outlook mailbox or an agency export starts it. The read, the match and the batch line run on their own. The accountant gates every flagged line and releases the batch.
lenses.ambitious: Give the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo site leads a same-week list of blocked flex invoices, which they do not receive today. Demand for that list would grow in peak season, when flex headcount moves between 150 and 300, if it were cheap to produce.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss re-typing PDFs or hunting a portal for a surcharge code. The work to keep is the real dispute with a site or an agency, and a batch that can be signed without rework.
lenses.options: Two codings of one haulier invoice, domestic VAT or reverse charge, and two sites for the same agency hours, change what is paid this week and which site carries the cost. The accountant picks the draft before release.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes an exception queue and a batch sign-off, with the right to hold a site's flex invoices until the hours are agreed. The job is more expert on VAT, agency disputes and tax payments.
reach: The bookkeeper's match of staffing-agency invoices to approved hours, once the accountant learns how each agency's portal states a shift and a surcharge.
The bookkeeper's VAT coding on routine purchase invoices, once the accountant can maintain the reverse-charge rules the bookkeepers hit.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to judge a disputed hour sheet, a changed IBAN, a VAT treatment the match cannot show, and any tax assessment that must agree to the filed return, and has to release the money. Agency invoices name flex workers, so a wrong or leaked file is an AVG matter as well as a bad payment.
tasks.pattern_why: Portal files and PDFs are messy. One model call turns each file into supplier, amount, VAT code, IBAN and site, which AFAS can then match with rules. The path is known, so an open-ended agent is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice lands in the AFAS purchase inbox, the Outlook invoices mailbox, or an agency portal export.
steps: A model call reads the file and proposes supplier, amount, VAT code, IBAN, site and account, with the source file attached.
AFAS matches the proposal to the purchase order, the receipt or the approved flex hours.
Clean matches wait in the payment batch.
New IBANs, amount mismatches, missing hours and reverse-charge doubts go to the accountant's queue.
The accountant clears the queue and releases the Rabobank batch, or sends it back.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant releases each Rabobank batch and clears every flagged invoice, fee and tax payment before money leaves.
data_needed: Invoice file, amount and IBAN
Purchase order and receipt
Approved flex hours by site
VAT code and reverse-charge flag
Vendor master, payment mandate and the filed tax return for assessments
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS invoice, the match result and the Rabobank batch number, with the source file stored in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Dutch B2B e-invoicing is planned from 1 July 2030 and reporting from 1 July 2031, and is not law yet. A PDF is not an e-invoice, so Noordhaven's invoices stay messy files until that regime is real.
Intra-EU and reverse-charge invoices are due within 10 days under the ViDA discussion, and whether that deadline applies to domestic invoices is still open.
A four-eye release on the payment batch, plus a hard stop on a changed IBAN, is a control that can be written down. Clean matches can wait in the batch while flagged lines wait for a person.

risks: A wrong IBAN or a duplicated agency invoice can sit inside a batch that is reviewed mainly by total.
Flex worker names and hours on agency invoices are personal data. An external model needs a processor agreement, and the invoice text must not be kept for training.
A reverse-charge code that is wrong or late becomes a VAT filing error, and the domestic deadline is still unsettled.
The same accountant editing the match rule and releasing the Rabobank batch weakens segregation of duties.
research_questions: What share of last quarter's payments were clean AFAS matches, PDF or portal invoices, agency invoices, and tax or fee assessments?
How often were flex hours disputed, and how many days did those invoices sit before payment?
Does the payment mandate allow release after exception review, or must a person open every invoice?
Will the three agencies send a stable hours file under a data-processing term that covers names, shifts and surcharges?

tasks.short: Check the monthly figures and statements against the close standards.

today.trigger: The month closes, or the Finance Director asks whether the figures are fit to use in the forecast.
steps: Export the trial balance, subledgers and the prior month from AFAS.
Tie the statements to the ledger and to the nightly Power BI extract.
Review material lines against the close checklist and the usual site pattern for labour, flex and transport.
Trace a break to a journal, an invoice or an accrual.
Write the exceptions for the controller and the Finance Director.
drudgery: Ticking lines that have not moved.
Rebuilding the same tie-out workbook each month.
Hunting a missing piece across mail and the bookkeepers' files.
today.time_sinks: Site temp-labour and claims that arrive after the first draft, and the manual tie between AFAS and the nightly Power BI extract.

lenses.faster: The tie-out and the list of lines that moved are ready when the accountant sits down. Reading material lines, judging conformance and accepting the pack still take about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar and the nightly AFAS extract start it. The draft tie-out and the movement list run before anyone opens them. The pack is issued only after the accountant accepts it.
lenses.ambitious: Give the FP&A analysts a weekly completeness note per site for temp labour, overtime and claims, so the forecast meets fewer month-end surprises. They would ask for it every reforecast week if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking balances that did not change. The work to keep is the hour with the Finance Director on a figure that moves profit or the forecast.
lenses.options: Two treatments of the same claim, on the site or held centrally, change the site result the business will see. The accountant chooses from those drafts before the pack goes out.
lenses.altitude: The week starts from a tie-out that has already passed or failed, and the accountant can hold the pack until a material line is explained. The work is more expert, centred on presentation and on which figures the business can trust.
reach: The controller's first review of the monthly management pack, once the accountant learns which lines the Finance Director uses in the forecast.
The FP&A analyst's check that site actuals tie to the ledger before a reforecast, once the accountant learns the forecast categories.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to decide whether the statements meet the company's Dutch reporting practice and whether a figure is fit for the Finance Director. Tested models do well at file search and following instructions, and they still fail on judgement across files. The sources do not cover Dutch GAAP.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call can turn the ledger extract and the close checklist into a tie-out and a list of breaks that can be checked line by line. The route is fixed, so an agent is unnecessary. The accountant accepts the pack before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar opens the reporting step, or the nightly AFAS extract lands.
steps: The job pulls the trial balance, subledgers and the Power BI extract for the same timestamp.
A model call drafts the tie-out, the lines that moved, and the breaks against the checklist.
Each drafted figure carries the AFAS account and journal it came from.
The accountant reviews material lines, site labour, flex and transport, and rejects any line that does not trace.
The accepted pack goes to the controller and the Finance Director.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant accepts the pack, line by line where it is material, before the controller or the Finance Director relies on it.
data_needed: Trial balance and subledgers at a named timestamp
Prior month and the close checklist
Power BI extract from the same night
Materiality thresholds agreed with the controller
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close binder, with the AFAS timestamp, the draft, the accept or reject, and the accountant's name.

evidence.claim: On four month-end scenarios, twelve licensed CPAs with about 5.5 years' experience averaged about 37%, and the tested model scored 100% on 20 attempts. The tasks were detail, file search and following instructions. Client questions and tacit context were left out, and the study says accountants are not shown to be replaceable.

On 160 US GAAP tasks the leading result met 61.8% of criteria, and 58% were never fully solved in eight attempts. Judgement is the bottleneck, and multi-step reasoning is over half of the top model's errors. The sample is a US law firm on QuickBooks.
Across 79 small and mid-sized firms, accountants using AI closed 7.5 days faster and served 55% more clients a week. 62% of 277 surveyed accountants worry about errors.
evidence.source: CFO Dive on Choi and Xie, 13 Aug 2025, https://www.cfodive.com/news/ai-cuts-monthly-financial-close-time-75-days-mit-stanford-study-accounting-accountants/757610/

evidence.claim: No benchmark in the sources covers Dutch GAAP, Dutch VAT or a statutory audit file. A pack for Noordhaven can be drafted and tied to AFAS, and conformance to Dutch reporting practice stays untested.

risks: A draft can add an assumption that is not in the ledger, so the pack cannot be rebuilt from AFAS.
A US GAAP or QuickBooks result can look finished and still be wrong under Dutch reporting practice.
The nightly Power BI extract can miss a same-day journal, so the tie-out agrees to a stale file.
Audit adjustments are an input metric for this team. A silent miss on a material line damages the forecast the business is asked to trust.
research_questions: On last month's file, what share of drafted tie-out lines match AFAS to the cent with no added assumption?
Which statement lines does the external auditor always re-perform, and which would they accept from this pack?
How many hours go to building the workbook, and how many to judging material lines?
Does a weekly site completeness note change an FP&A forecast decision?

tasks.short: Reconcile ledger accounts to the bank, subledgers and control accounts.

today.trigger: A Rabobank statement arrives, a subledger drifts from the general ledger, or the close checklist reaches reconciliations.
steps: Import the Rabobank statement and the AFAS open items.
Match bank lines, accounts payable, accounts receivable and the VAT control account.
List timing differences, missing invoices and unknown receipts.
Clear what the documents explain and draft a journal for the rest.
Leave material unexplained items for the close review.
drudgery: Matching bank lines that repeat every week.
Copying open items into Excel.
Rebuilding the same reconciliation layout each month.
today.time_sinks: Unknown receipts, agency invoices posted to the wrong site, and items that sit until close week because nobody owns them earlier.

lenses.faster: Matched lines and a first draft of each remaining break are done before the review. Unexplained items and the approval of each clearing entry still take a bit under half of today's effort.
lenses.autonomous: The Rabobank statement and the nightly AFAS open items start it. The match and the draft workpaper run unattended. Each clearing entry waits for the accountant.
lenses.ambitious: Decide each morning whether to chase a small bank or agency-control break, including night-shift items that today wait until close week. Site leads would use a daily open list in peak season if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss lining up bank lines that already agree. The work to keep is the break that shows a leak, a mis-coded site, or a receipt nobody has claimed.
lenses.options: Two clearing drafts for the same break, a timing difference or a cost on the site, change the month's result. The accountant picks the draft the bank line and the AFAS entry support.
lenses.altitude: The accountant works a daily exception list and can stop the close on an open material break. The job is more expert on the breaks that move profit.
reach: The bookkeeper's supplier-statement reconciliation, once the accountant can clear AFAS accounts-payable open items against supplier statements.
The credit and collections officer's match of incoming Rabobank receipts to open customer items, once the accountant learns the order-to-cash dispute codes.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to say what an unmatched amount is: timing, a missing accrual, a miscode, or something to escalate. That call changes the books. The machine can list the break and draft the wording.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching a CAMT.053 bank file or a subledger to the ledger is a rule. One model call then writes the reason and the clearing draft for what remains, tied to the source keys. The accountant approves the workpaper before anything posts.

in_practice.trigger: A Rabobank CAMT.053 statement arrives, or the nightly AFAS open-item extract shows a control account out of balance.
steps: Rules match bank lines and subledger items to AFAS on amount, reference and counterparty.
Unmatched items are grouped into timing, missing document, wrong site and unknown.
A model call drafts the reconciliation and a clearing journal, each line citing the bank reference and the AFAS key.
The accountant accepts, corrects or escalates each open break.
Accepted clearances post, and material open items stay on the close list.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves each clearing journal and every reconciliation with a material open item before it posts or is treated as finished.
data_needed: CAMT.053 statement
AFAS open items for bank, payables, receivables and VAT control
Supplier statements and agency invoices still open
Materiality limit for a break that can wait
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS journal and the SharePoint reconciliation, storing the statement id, the match keys, the draft and the approval.

evidence.claim: Bank and subledger matches follow amounts, references and counterparties a program can apply to a CAMT.053 file. The open break still needs a written reason and a person before a clearing entry posts.

On 160 US GAAP tasks, multi-step reasoning across files is over half of the top model's errors, and 58% of tasks were never fully solved in eight attempts. A break that spans the bank file, an agency invoice and the ledger is that kind of task.
Month-end scenarios where models beat experienced CPAs rewarded detail, file search and following instructions, and left out asking the right questions and building tacit context.

risks: An automatic clear labelled as timing can hide a duplicate payment or a loss.
A written reason that does not cite the bank line and the AFAS entry cannot be audited.
Night-shift and flex items often have no purchase order, so peak months will over-flag.
Taking on customer-receipt matching while also releasing supplier payments weakens segregation of duties.
research_questions: What percentage of Rabobank lines and subledger items matched with no human last quarter?
How many open breaks were material at the last three closes, and how old were they?
Can every draft clearing entry store the bank reference and the AFAS key it came from?
Which euro limit would the controller accept for a break that waits, and which breaks must be cleared before the close?

tasks.short: Inspect the books and the AFAS setup against our procedures.

today.trigger: The controller schedules a controls review, the auditor asks how a process works, or the same accounts keep failing at close.
steps: Read the procedure on SharePoint and the authorisation matrix in AFAS.
Sample journals, invoices and master-data changes.
Check segregation of duties, numbering and whether the chart was used as written.
Note workarounds the sites use for shift premiums and flex cost.
Report the gaps to the controller.
drudgery: Sampling folders by hand.
Exporting user rights into Excel.
Repeating a test the auditor asked for last year.
today.time_sinks: Understanding a warehouse workaround that is not in the procedure, and rewriting the finding so the controller can act on it.

lenses.faster: Pulling samples and ticking whether a recorded step happened disappears. Judging whether the procedure works, and writing what should change, still takes about three fifths of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly run starts from the AFAS transaction and rights log. Tests score every posting, user-right change and IBAN edit. The accountant decides which failures are reported as real gaps.
lenses.ambitious: Send the Finance Director and the works council a quarterly note on whether flex cost and shift premiums followed the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO. Demand would grow around peak season and CAO talks if the note were cheap to refresh.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pulling samples that show nothing. The work to keep is a failed procedure in a warehouse, and the fix agreed with the people who run it.
lenses.options: A narrow test pack, limited to duplicates and IBAN changes, and a wider one that adds segregation of duties and CAO premium codes, lead the Finance Director to close different gaps this quarter. The accountant chooses the pack.
lenses.altitude: The accountant reviews an exception list drawn from every transaction and can declare a procedure failed on that evidence, and require a fix before the next close. The job is more expert on control design.
reach: The controller's test of segregation of duties on payments and journals, once the accountant learns the AFAS authorisation matrix and the four-eye rule.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to judge whether a failed test is a harmless shortcut or a hole in the books, and has to talk to the site about how the workaround actually runs. A test cannot decide that the system is effective. Interviews stay with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: Duplicates, segregation-of-duties clashes, IBAN changes and postings outside the written procedure are pass-or-fail tests over AFAS data. The accountant judges effectiveness from the failures. No model call is required to run the tests.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly AFAS log of journals, invoices and master-data changes is available, or the controller opens a review.
steps: Tests run on every posting for duplicates, authorisation clashes, IBAN edits and accounts outside the procedure.
Failures land on one list with the user, the time, the amount and the account.
The accountant marks each failure as harmless, a procedure breach, or something to escalate.
A short note to the controller states the breaches and the fix before the next close.
The same tests stay on for the next week so the fix can be seen.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant decides which failures are reported and which fix is required. A test result alone does not change a procedure or a person's authorisation.
data_needed: Journal and invoice log with user, time, account and amount
Authorisation matrix and IBAN change log
Written procedures and the chart
CAO premium codes payroll already uses
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint controls file, with the test version, the population, the failures and the accountant's marking.

evidence.claim: Duplicate postings, segregation-of-duties clashes and IBAN changes can be tested on every AFAS transaction with rules. Whether the accounting system is effective still depends on a person reading the failures and the warehouse practice behind them.

On 160 US GAAP tasks, judgement is the bottleneck and 58% were never fully solved in eight attempts. Inspecting a system for effectiveness is a judgement task, even when the underlying tests are mechanical.

risks: A test pack that records how fast each bookkeeper works becomes staff monitoring, and needs the works council before it runs.
Tight thresholds will flood the queue in peak season, when flex and shift volumes spike.
CAO premium rules are only partly machine-checkable. A false pass would mislead the works council.
The accountant who writes the test and who posts the journals should not be the only person who can mark a failure as harmless.
research_questions: Which AFAS tables record user, time, account and amount for every journal and master-data change?
How many exceptions did a shadow run of duplicate, segregation-of-duties and IBAN tests raise on one closed month?
Which procedures are written clearly enough to become a test without a rewrite?
Does the works council want findings on shift-premium coding, and under what information right?

tasks.short: Prepare the month-end accruals, prepayments and other adjustments.

today.trigger: The close checklist reaches accruals, or a prepayment, a claim or a payroll figure has to be brought into the month.
steps: Collect flex hours not yet invoiced, open claims, prepayments and payroll totals from AFAS.
Calculate vakantiegeld, shift premiums and other CAO accruals from the payroll figures.
Draft the journal with the basis and the reversal date.
Tie the draft to the ledger and to the forecast categories FP&A uses.
Post after review, with the controller on material amounts.
drudgery: Rolling prepaid schedules forward by hand.
Copying flex hours into Excel.
Retyping last month's accrual with a new date.
today.time_sinks: Waiting for agency hours and for payroll to close, then debating the flex accrual with FP&A late in the close.

lenses.faster: Building the schedule and drafting the journal leave the accountant's desk. Checking the basis, the CAO amounts and the material estimates still takes about two fifths of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: The accrual step on the close checklist, or a weekly flex-hour file, starts it. The draft journal and its tie-out run unattended. The accountant approves every entry before AFAS posts it.
lenses.ambitious: Accrue temp labour and open transport claims every week for the FP&A forecast, a decision the company now makes only at month end. FP&A would use that weekly accrual on every reforecast if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rolling the prepaid sheet forward by hand. The work to keep is the judgement on what the company actually owes for flex, claims and CAO pay.
lenses.options: Three drafts for uninvoiced flex, based on ordered hours, site-approved hours, or last month's run-rate, change profit and the forecast. The accountant picks the draft the evidence supports.
lenses.altitude: Accrual day becomes a review of drafts that already tie, and the accountant can put a weekly flex accrual into the forecast the sites will see. The job is more expert on estimates.
reach: The payroll specialist's monthly wage-accrual checklist, once the accountant learns CAO shift premiums, vakantiegeld and sick pay under the Wet verbetering poortwachter.
The FP&A analyst's weekly temp-labour input to the forecast, once the accountant learns how the forecast treats flex and reversals.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to stand behind an estimate when flex is not yet billed, a claim is open, or sick pay and vakantiegeld depend on facts payroll has not finished. Tax-related estimates stay on a human review. A journal that balances is still wrong if the basis is wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call can draft the journal, the basis and the reversal from the schedules and the hour files, with each figure tied to a source. The accountant approves each entry before it posts. An agent is unnecessary because the close step is known.

in_practice.trigger: The close checklist opens accruals, or a weekly file of approved flex hours and open claims arrives.
steps: Schedules for prepayments, payroll CAO amounts, uninvoiced flex and open claims are read from AFAS and the agency files.
A model call drafts the journal, the reversal date and a basis line that cites each source figure.
The draft ties to the forecast categories and to the accounts it will hit.
The accountant accepts or rewrites each entry and its basis.
AFAS posts only the accepted journals, and the reversal is dated.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves every adjusting journal before it posts. Material amounts also go past the controller. Tax estimates are always in that human review.
data_needed: Approved flex hours not yet invoiced, by site
Open claims and prepaid schedules
Payroll totals for vakantiegeld, shift premiums and sick pay
Forecast categories and reversal rules
Controller's threshold for a second approval
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS journal number and the SharePoint accrual file, with the source figures, the draft, the approval and the reversal date.

evidence.claim: Workday's Accounting Agent extracts contract details, prepares entries and recommends revenue schedules, and the teams stay responsible for review. Noordhaven's ledger is AFAS Profit. The sources describe no equivalent AFAS agent for adjusting journals.
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list for finance teams using AI agents.
On four month-end scenarios, a model beat experienced CPAs on detail, file search and following instructions. Asking the right questions and tacit context were outside the test.
Multi-step reasoning is over half of the leading model's errors on 160 US GAAP tasks. An accrual that chains payroll, agency hours and a reversal is exposed to that failure.

risks: A balanced journal can rest on an assumption nobody can trace to a source file.
A weekly flex accrual double-counts the cost once the agency invoice arrives, if the reversal rule is loose.
CAO and Wet verbetering poortwachter amounts that touch pay need payroll's figures. A finance-only estimate can conflict with the payslip.
Posting every small draft would bury the review that protects audit adjustments.
research_questions: What share of last quarter's adjustments were recurring schedules, and what share were estimates?
On a shadow month, how many draft journals tied to source lines with no added assumption?
Does FP&A change a forecast decision when the flex accrual is refreshed weekly?
Above which amount does the controller want to approve an accrual personally?

tasks.short: Direct the bookkeepers on filing, recording and sending the close file.

today.trigger: Close week starts, a VAT or filing deadline approaches, or a bookkeeper is blocked on a record.
steps: Issue the close checklist to the three bookkeepers.
Check what has been recorded, filed on SharePoint and sent.
Reassign work when a site file or an agency file is late.
Confirm the VAT, payment and ledger packs are complete.
Prepare the statutory pack for SBR filing with the KVK, which AFAS does not send for a large company.
drudgery: Status mail that only asks whether a step is done.
Updating the checklist in Excel.
Asking again for the same missing document.
today.time_sinks: Waiting on people, and the year-end SBR pack that has to be assembled outside AFAS for the KVK.

lenses.faster: Status mail and rebuilding the checklist shrink. Deciding who does what, and unblocking a person, stay with the accountant and take about seven tenths of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar opens the checklist. Status against AFAS, missing documents and reminder drafts build on their own. The accountant directs the people and decides what is sent.
lenses.ambitious: Give the statutory auditor a standing index of the close file at interim and at year-end, in place of today's one-off scramble. The auditor would ask for the interim pull as well if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the mail that only asks if a step is done. The work to keep is the short decision that unblocks a bookkeeper or settles two deadlines that collide.
lenses.options: Two sequences, VAT and bank first, or the agency accrual first, change what the bookkeepers can finish before day three and what the Finance Director sees. The accountant sets the sequence.
lenses.altitude: The accountant directs from a checklist that already shows blockers, and can reassign a close task and hold transmission until the file is complete. The job stays a skilled job about people, deadlines and accountability.
reach: The controller's day-to-day chase of the close calendar, once the accountant learns which dates, including the VAT return and the KVK filing, cannot move.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to set priority, judge workload and speak to the bookkeepers, the controller and the auditor. A reminder draft does not carry accountability. A tool that scores how fast a named person works is a works council matter.
tasks.pattern_why: The checklist order can be drafted, and the accountant remains the person who directs the bookkeepers. Status and reminders are assistance. An agent must not assign work or mark a filing as sent.

in_practice.trigger: The close calendar reaches a filing or recording step, or an AFAS task on the checklist passes its due time.
steps: The checklist shows each step as open, blocked or done, from AFAS status and the SharePoint file list.
A draft reminder names the missing document and the deadline, for the accountant to send.
The accountant reassigns work, changes the sequence, or chases the site that is blocking a bookkeeper.
The accountant confirms which packs are complete enough to transmit.
The SBR pack for the KVK is ticked only when the file has actually been filed outside AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant decides priorities, sends the chasers, and is the person who allows a pack to be transmitted. The checklist does not assign work on its own.
data_needed: Close calendar and statutory dates
AFAS status of journals, VAT and payments
SharePoint file list for the close binder
Names of the bookkeepers responsible for each step
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close checklist, with status changes, who approved transmission, and the KVK filing reference when it exists.

evidence.claim: Large companies file their accounts with the KVK via SBR from financial year 2025, and AFAS cannot file this for them. The transmission step stays outside the ledger system.
Directing filing staff is coordination. A status draft can show what is missing. The decision on priority and the accountability for what is sent stay with the accountant.
Firms using AI closed 7.5 days faster, and 62% of 277 surveyed accountants still worry about errors. A faster checklist does not remove the need for a person to judge whether the file is fit to send.
evidence.source: CFO Dive on Choi and Xie, 13 Aug 2025, https://www.cfodive.com/news/ai-cuts-monthly-financial-close-time-75-days-mit-stanford-study-accounting-accountants/757610/

risks: Reminder logs can become individual performance monitoring. The works council should see the design before it runs.
A checklist that marks a KVK filing as done inside AFAS would be false, because AFAS cannot file SBR for a large company.
Automatic chasers will hit sites during night shifts and peak weeks if they ignore the real blocker.
A tool that ranks bookkeepers could fall under worker-monitoring duties in the EU AI Act. That classification needs a legal check before build.
research_questions: How many close-week hours go to status chasing, and how many to real priority decisions?
Which filing steps does AFAS complete, and which does the SBR path to the KVK still require by hand?
Will the works council accept a checklist that shows task status and does not record a person's speed?
Would the statutory auditor use an interim file index, and which documents must it contain?

tasks.short: Maintain the chart of accounts and code each entry to the right account.

today.trigger: A new cost appears, a supplier is miscoded, or the chart no longer matches how the sites and the forecast work.
steps: Look up the chart and the coding guide in AFAS or on SharePoint.
Assign the entry to an account, a cost centre and a VAT code.
Correct batches of miscoded agency or transport lines.
Propose a new account when nothing on the chart fits.
Update the guide the bookkeepers use.
drudgery: Coding the same supplier from memory.
Fixing last month's miscodes in a batch.
Keeping a private Excel guide that the bookkeepers do not see.
today.time_sinks: Peak-season agency lines and foreign hauliers, where the right account and the reverse-charge code are easy to get wrong.

lenses.faster: A proposal for account, site and VAT code is attached before the accountant looks. Accepting a familiar line is quick. New accounts and odd transport or agency costs still take about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A journal or an invoice with no confirmed account starts it. The proposal is attached before posting. The accountant approves new accounts and any coding the written guide does not already allow.
lenses.ambitious: Give FP&A a split of temp labour by site and by shift, including night shift, so the forecast can see Venlo's nights on their own. FP&A would ask for finer splits on the next planning cycle if maintaining them were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss re-coding the same agency from memory. The work to keep is a chart that shows the three sites cleanly, and the call on a cost that does not fit.
lenses.options: Parking night-shift flex on the general temp-labour account, or opening a site-and-shift account, changes what FP&A can forecast. The accountant chooses from those chart drafts with the controller.
lenses.altitude: Coding becomes a review of proposals. The accountant can open an account the forecast will use and can reject a coding that muddies a site. The job is more expert on the structure of the ledger.
reach: The bookkeeper's day-to-day account coding on purchase invoices, once the accountant maintains the cost centres the sites actually use.
The FP&A analyst's mapping from ledger accounts to forecast lines, once the accountant learns the planning model.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to decide that a new account earns its place and still maps to the Dutch reporting lines the auditor expects. A proposal does not see that a finer chart for FP&A will burden the bookkeepers or break that mapping.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call can propose the account, the site and the VAT code against the written chart, with the guide line it used. Opening or retiring an account is a separate decision the accountant approves before anyone posts to it.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice or journal has no confirmed account, or a bookkeeper asks for a code that is not in the guide.
steps: The written chart, VAT codes and site cost centres are read from AFAS.
A model call proposes the account, cost centre and VAT code, and cites the guide line or the similar past entry.
Proposals the guide already covers are shown as a one-click accept.
Anything new, any reverse-charge doubt and any new account wait for the accountant.
Accepted accounts are added to the SharePoint guide the bookkeepers use.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves each new account and each coding the guide does not already allow, before the entry posts.
data_needed: Current chart, cost centres and VAT codes
Coding guide and recent corrections
Supplier and agency master
FP&A forecast lines by site
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS entry and the SharePoint coding guide, with the proposal, the guide line cited, and the accept or reject.

evidence.claim: Workday's Accounting Agent prepares proposed entries from source documents and leaves review with the team. That is evidence the pattern exists in a product. It is not evidence that AFAS Profit proposes account codes.

Judgement and multi-step reasoning, not retrieval, drive the errors on 160 US GAAP tasks, where 58% were never fully solved in eight attempts. Choosing an account that also has to serve Dutch statements and the forecast is that kind of judgement.
A coding proposal is checkable when it cites the chart line it used. A new account still changes later closes and the audit mapping, so it waits for a person.

risks: Accepted proposals can hide a reverse-charge error until the VAT return.
A finer chart slows the close if every new account needs a tie-out the team does not have time for.
Bulk-accepting wrong accounts would raise audit adjustments, which this role is measured on.
A guide that lives in an external model, and diverges from AFAS, recreates the private Excel the bookkeepers already miss.
research_questions: What share of entries last quarter used a supplier default, and what share were recoded at close?
Which missing splits, by site or by shift, would change an FP&A forecast line?
Can a proposal store the chart line or the past entry it relied on?
Does the controller want to approve every new account, or only accounts that change the external statements?

tasks.short: Design, change and document how the books are kept in AFAS.

today.trigger: A close step keeps failing, the auditor comments on the file, or a coming change such as e-invoicing or a site split needs a system change.
steps: Describe the gap in the current AFAS setup, the Excel beside it, or the Power BI feed.
Agree the change with the controller and, where pay data is involved, with payroll.
Configure AFAS or the extract the dashboards read.
Test the change on a closed month.
Write the procedure on SharePoint and walk the bookkeepers through it.
drudgery: Rewriting procedures in Word from scratch.
Clicking through AFAS to reconstruct a setting nobody wrote down.
Maintaining a parallel Excel process the ledger does not know about.
today.time_sinks: Configuration work without a safe test company in AFAS, and the SBR filing path that sits outside AFAS.

lenses.faster: First drafts of procedures, test lists and configuration notes take less time. Deciding the design, configuring AFAS and checking the audit trail still take about two thirds of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A repeated close failure, an audit comment, or a dated legal change opens a change note. Drafts of the procedure, the tests and the setting list wait for review. The accountant decides what is switched on.
lenses.ambitious: Give the FP&A analysts a nightly ledger feed the forecast can read, covering the lines they still take from a shadow Excel. They would ask for more lines each planning round if adding one were cheap and the tie-out held.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping a procedure that already lives in someone's head. The work to keep is the design of a control that makes the close shorter and the forecast traceable to AFAS.
lenses.options: One accrual account for all three agencies, or one account per agency and site, changes how fast a break is found and how heavy the chart becomes. The accountant chooses the design before anyone configures AFAS.
lenses.altitude: System work becomes a short list of design choices, each with a drafted test. The accountant can refuse a shortcut that breaks the audit trail or the four-eye rule. The job is more expert on design, and the accountant stays accountable for what goes live.
reach: The controller's write-up of the finance process for the statutory auditor, once the accountant learns the audit-file index.
The FP&A analyst's shadow Excel for actuals, once the accountant learns which forecast lines must come from AFAS only.

tasks.human_edge: The accountant has to choose the design the controller, the auditor and the bookkeepers can live with, and has to refuse a change that weakens segregation of duties. A drafted procedure is not a decision to switch it on.
tasks.pattern_why: The accountant leads the design. A model can draft the procedure, the test list and the configuration note inside a fixed change template. The change counts only after the accountant and the controller accept it in AFAS.

in_practice.trigger: The same close step fails twice, the auditor writes a comment, or a fixed date such as the e-invoicing timetable forces a design choice.
steps: A change note states the gap, the AFAS settings involved and the forecast or filing line affected.
A model call drafts the procedure, the test list and the setting note from the current SharePoint process and the AFAS screen names.
The accountant and the controller pick the design, including segregation of duties.
The change is tried on a closed month in a test environment, then switched on in the live company.
The accepted procedure replaces the old one on SharePoint, and the bookkeepers are shown the difference.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant and the controller both accept the design before it is switched on in the live AFAS company. A draft procedure has no effect on its own.
data_needed: Current AFAS settings and the authorisation matrix
Close failures and audit comments
Forecast lines still taken from Excel
The filing path for SBR, which sits outside AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint change log, with the design choice, the test result on a named closed month, and the two approvals.

evidence.claim: Large companies must file accounts with the KVK via SBR from financial year 2025, and AFAS cannot file this for them. Recordkeeping design has to include a path outside AFAS.
The cabinet has chosen B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and transaction reporting from 1 July 2031. The choice is not law yet. A PDF is not an e-invoice.

Guidance on shadow AI in accounting describes a tool beside the ledger adding an assumption the workpaper cannot rebuild. A parallel Excel or an unlogged model prompt creates that risk for Noordhaven.
No source shows an AFAS agent that configures the general ledger. Drafting a procedure is assistance. Switching on a setting remains a human change in the live company.

risks: A change tested in the wrong AFAS environment can post into the live year.
Procedure text that includes flex worker names or hours needs an AVG check before it is sent to an external model.
Building an e-invoice format before the law is final can lock in a design the 2030 rules will not accept.
A system change that logs how named staff record journals needs a works council look, and may need an EU AI Act check if it is used to assess workers.
research_questions: Which recordkeeping changes in the last year were AFAS configuration, and which were Excel beside the ledger?
Does AFAS provide a test company that cannot post into the live year?
Which forecast lines does FP&A still take from Excel, and how far do they drift from AFAS?
What would the works council need to see if a new log records who posts which journal?

role.altitude: The week moves from posting and rechecking entries to setting the tie-outs, coding rules and tests that run on every entry, then telling the Finance Director which breaks change the result. The accountant gains the right to hold a payment batch, a journal and the close pack when a tie-out fails, and the right to put a weekly flex accrual into the forecast. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The bookkeeper's routine coding of supplier and agency invoices, once the accountant maintains the match rules and the VAT codes.
The bookkeeper's supplier-statement reconciliation, once the accountant can clear AFAS open items against Rabobank lines.
The controller's first-pass close tie-out, once the accountant can explain a material variance in the figures the Finance Director uses.
The FP&A analyst's actuals check on temp labour and transport before a reforecast, once the accountant can split those costs by site and shift.

The payroll specialist's wage-accrual inputs for vakantiegeld, shift premiums and sick pay, once the accountant learns the CAO figures and the Wet verbetering poortwachter amounts payroll already calculates.
role.ceiling_note: Two accountants cannot take the three bookkeepers' daily volume, the controller's signature, or the Finance Director's forecast call. These eight tasks are about two fifths of the role. Tax positions, contact with the Belastingdienst, audit interviews and advice to management sit outside this design. Close week stays bound by the VAT deadline, by SBR filing that AFAS does not send to the KVK, and by the need for a named person the works council and the auditor can question. No source here tests Dutch GAAP, Dutch VAT or a statutory audit file.
skills_to_grow: Writing match rules, tie-outs and test thresholds that can run on AFAS every night
Dutch reporting practice, enough to defend a statement line to the controller and the auditor
VAT on domestic and intra-EU transport, reverse charge, and the e-invoicing dates of 1 July 2030 and 1 July 2031
CAO accruals: shift premiums, vakantiegeld, and sick pay under the Wet verbetering poortwachter
Tracing every drafted figure to an AFAS line, a bank reference or a source file
Reading which forecast lines FP&A needs, so the chart and the accruals serve the forecast
Works council and AVG limits when a tool logs staff work or reads flex worker names
role.ambitious_version: The accountant keeps a close the business can query during the month. Flex labour and transport claims are accrued weekly for FP&A. Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo see blocked agency invoices in the same week. Routine payments, matches and control tests run on written rules. The accountant spends the freed hours on the estimates, the chart and the breaks that change profit, with a file the auditor can follow and a CAO coding note the works council can read.
